title: Domino's Pepperoni Pizza
description: The classic crowd-pleaser: a generous layer of pepperoni over 100% real mozzarella and signature tomato sauce, on your choice of crust.
fullContent:
The Pizza Everybody Orders First

Let's start with the obvious: the Pepperoni Pizza is the most-ordered item at Domino's, and honestly, it earns that spot. There's nothing fancy going on here, and that's precisely the point. You get the signature tomato sauce, a proper layer of 100% real mozzarella, and pepperoni that curls and crisps at the edges in the oven. Simple, consistent, and it never lets you down. Whether it's a solo dinner in front of the TV or the anchor of a big family order, pepperoni just works. Every single time.

Ask ten people their go-to Domino's order and most of them will say pepperoni without even pausing. That kind of loyalty doesn't happen by accident — it happens because the pizza is reliably good and endlessly flexible. You can keep it plain, load it up, or use it as the safe pick alongside something more adventurous for the table.

Picking the Right Crust

Here's where a lot of people order on autopilot and miss out. Pepperoni tastes genuinely different depending on the crust underneath it, so it's worth a moment's thought.

CrustWhat You GetBest For
Hand TossedSoft, pillowy, the classicMost people, most nights
Handmade PanThick, buttery, indulgentWhen you want a treat
Crunchy ThinLight, crisp, less breadLetting the pepperoni shine
Brooklyn StyleBig, foldable slicesThat New York vibe
Gluten FreeSmall size onlyAvoiding wheat

My honest pick? Hand Tossed for a crowd, Crunchy Thin when I want the pepperoni to be the star rather than the dough. There's no wrong answer, but there's definitely a right one for your mood. If you want the full rundown on which size to pair with it, the pizza sizes guide lays it all out.

How to Order It for Less

Never pay full menu price for a pepperoni. I mean it. It's one of the items that almost always qualifies for a deal, so grab it through Mix & Match or the $6.99 Each promo and you'll routinely pay less than the sticker price. A Large Pepperoni inside a two-item deal frequently costs less than ordering it alone, which feels almost backwards until you get used to it. Check the current coupons first, choose carryout to skip the delivery fee, and make sure you're signed into Domino's Rewards so it banks points toward a free pizza down the line.

What's Actually In It (Nutrition & Allergens)

Let's be straight about the nutrition, because pizza is a treat and pretending otherwise helps nobody. A single slice of a Large Hand Tossed Pepperoni runs roughly 290 to 320 calories depending on how it's portioned. The pizza contains wheat and milk, and the pepperoni is a pork product, so it isn't suitable for vegetarian, halal, or kosher diets. If you're watching calories, asking for light cheese or going Crunchy Thin trims things down noticeably. And if wheat's the concern, the Gluten Free crust is there, though Domino's makes it in a shared kitchen, so it suits a preference more than a serious medical allergy.

Make It Your Own

The plain pepperoni is a blank canvas, and half the fun is tweaking it. Extra pepperoni is the obvious move for the devoted. Adding a second meat like Italian sausage turns it into something heartier. And if you find yourself wanting more going on, the loaded ExtravaganZZa is the natural next step up — same deal pricing, a lot more toppings. For families, my go-to trick is pairing one pepperoni with a plain cheese so the picky eaters stay happy. There's more of that thinking in the family picks guide.

Round Out the Meal

A pepperoni pizza rarely travels alone in my house. Add an order of Stuffed Cheesy Bread and it turns a pizza into a proper spread, and a 2-liter keeps everyone's cup full for cheap. Order the pizza and the side together through a deal and the whole thing stays friendly on the wallet.

The Bottom Line

The Pepperoni Pizza is popular because it's genuinely good, reliably consistent, and easy to make your own. Order it through a deal, pick the crust that matches your mood, and you've got a dinner that never disappoints. Just remember these are example prices — this is an independent, unofficial guide, so let the official Domino's app confirm the real total at checkout.

title: Domino's ExtravaganZZa Pizza
description: Domino's most loaded specialty pizza: pepperoni, ham, Italian sausage, beef, onions, green peppers, mushrooms and black olives with extra cheese.
fullContent:
The Everything Pizza

If plain pepperoni ever starts to feel a little boring, the ExtravaganZZa is your answer. This is Domino's take on the classic supreme, and it's the most loaded pizza on the whole specialty menu, no contest. We're talking a genuine pile-up of toppings on a single pie. It's the pizza you order when you want a bit of everything and you don't want to make any hard choices about what to leave off.

Here's what actually lands on it, because the name isn't exaggerating.

ToppingsThe Finish
Pepperoni, ham, Italian sausage, seasoned beefFour meats, seriously
Onions, green peppers, mushrooms, black olivesFour veggies for balance
Extra mozzarellaBecause of course

Eight toppings and extra cheese. That's not a pizza, that's a commitment, and I mean that as the highest compliment.

Who Should Order It

The ExtravaganZZa is made for two kinds of people. First, the die-hard meat lovers who measure a pizza by how much is going on. Second, and this is the underrated one, groups that can't agree on toppings. When everybody wants something different, a pizza that already has everything quietly settles the argument. Nobody's disappointed because a little bit of what they wanted is right there. Vegetarians are the exception here — you'll want the Pacific Veggie instead, which is a proper pizza in its own right rather than an afterthought.

Getting It for the Right Price

Because it carries a full load of premium toppings, the ExtravaganZZa sits above a plain two-topping on the menu. But here's the trick that changes everything: specialty pizzas usually qualify for Mix & Match at the same per-item price as a basic pie. So you get all those toppings for the price of a plain one. That's genuinely one of the best-value moves on the entire menu. Check the current deals, go carryout to dodge the fee, and stay in Domino's Rewards so even this pricier pizza banks points toward a free one.

Lightening It Up

Let's be honest about the nutrition, because with eight toppings and extra cheese, this is one of the higher-calorie pizzas Domino's makes. Expect roughly 320 to 360 calories per slice on a Large Hand Tossed. It contains wheat, milk and soy, and includes both pork and beef. If you want to enjoy it without the full weight, two easy levers help a lot: ask for light cheese, or order it on Crunchy Thin Crust. The thin crust in particular is great here — it cuts some dough and, weirdly, lets all those toppings shine even more. Win-win.

Building a Full Meal Around It

The ExtravaganZZa is hearty enough to headline a real spread. Pair it with Stuffed Cheesy Bread and a 2-liter and you've got a complete family dinner sorted. If you're feeding a mixed crowd, run one ExtravaganZZa for the adventurous eaters alongside a plain pepperoni for the purists — that combo covers just about everyone. The family picks guide has more combos like it.

The Bottom Line

The ExtravaganZZa is the pizza for people who don't want to choose. Loaded, satisfying, and surprisingly good value when you order it inside a deal. Just remember the prices here are examples — this is an independent, unofficial guide, so let the official Domino's app confirm the real total when you check out. Then dig in, because there's a lot going on with this one.

title: Domino's Philly Cheese Steak Pizza
description: Tender steak, fresh onions, green peppers and mushrooms over a creamy blend of American and provolone cheese instead of tomato sauce.
fullContent:
A Cheesesteak That Thinks It's a Pizza

Now here's something a little different. The Philly Cheese Steak Pizza throws out the rulebook and skips tomato sauce entirely. Instead, it's built on a creamy blend of American and provolone cheese, then loaded with tender steak, fresh onions, green peppers and mushrooms. The result? It tastes far more like an actual Philly cheesesteak sandwich than a traditional pizza. If you've ever found yourself a bit bored of red-sauce pizzas, this one's going to feel like a revelation.

What I really like about it is that it doesn't pretend to be something it's not. It leans all the way into the cheesesteak idea, and it commits. That confidence is exactly why it's built a loyal following among people who want their pizza to surprise them a little.

Why It Stands Out

Two things make this pizza genuinely different from almost everything else on the menu, and they matter more than you'd think.

What's DifferentWhy It Matters
No tomato saucePerfect if you're not a red-sauce fan
American + provolone baseRich, creamy, true cheesesteak flavor
Steak, no porkA solid pick for pork-free households

That last point deserves a mention. Because it's built on steak with no pork, the Philly Cheese Steak is a genuinely good option for households that skip pork — and it doesn't feel like a compromise while doing it.

The Best Way to Order It

Because the topping load is rich and cheesy, a lot of fans swear by the Crunchy Thin Crust here. It keeps the base crisp underneath all that provolone instead of going soft, and the contrast is lovely. Hand Tossed works fine too if you like it pillowy, but thin crust is the move I'd steer you toward for this particular pie. As for price, it's a specialty pizza, so it sits a bit higher on the menu — but it usually qualifies for Mix & Match, which drags it down to the same per-item rate as a basic pizza. Check the current deals before you order and you'll rarely pay full price.

Nutrition and Allergens, Honestly

Expect roughly 300 to 330 calories per Large slice, which is fairly reasonable for how rich it tastes. It contains wheat and milk — the milk comes from that double dose of cheese — and includes beef. As I mentioned, there's no pork, which some diners specifically look for. If you want to trim it down, the usual two tricks apply: ask for light cheese, or order it on thin crust. Both help without gutting the flavor.

What to Pair It With

The Philly Cheese Steak is savory and satisfying, so it plays well with something a little different alongside it. I'd pair it with Boneless Chicken and a drink through a deal, or add Stuffed Cheesy Bread for a proper two-item meal that fills the table. Since it's a bit of an adventurous pick, it also pairs nicely next to a plain pepperoni when you're feeding a mixed crowd.

The Bottom Line

The Philly Cheese Steak Pizza is for anyone craving something savory, cheesy, and refreshingly off the beaten path. No red sauce, no pork, all flavor. Order it thin-crust through a deal and you've got a genuinely different dinner without paying extra for the privilege. As always, these are example prices — this is an independent, unofficial guide, so let the official Domino's app confirm the real total at checkout.

faqs.answer: Tender Philly-style steak. There is no pork on this pizza, which makes it a good pick for diners avoiding pork.

title: Domino's Stuffed Cheesy Bread
description: Oven-baked bread stuffed with a blend of cheeses and seasoned with garlic and parsley, served with a dipping sauce.
fullContent:
The Side That Steals the Show

Let's give the sides their due, because Stuffed Cheesy Bread might be the best thing at Domino's that isn't technically a pizza. Here's the magic: it's soft, oven-baked bread with a blend of cheeses baked right inside, then brushed with garlic-and-parsley seasoning and cut into shareable strips. That inside part is the whole point. Plain bread twists put cheese on top; this stuffs it in, so every single piece pulls apart in that gooey, stringy way that makes everyone at the table reach for one more. It comes with marinara for dipping by default, and you can swap for garlic or ranch.

I'll be honest — I've ordered pizza plenty of times mostly as an excuse to also get the Stuffed Cheesy Bread. It's that good. If you're a first-timer at Domino's and you only try one side, make it this one.

The Varieties Worth Knowing

The original is the classic, but Domino's gives you a few ways to dress it up, and each one changes the vibe.

VarietyWhat's AddedGood For
OriginalJust the cheese blendPurists and picky eaters
Bacon & JalapeñoSmoky bacon, a little heatSpice fans (contains pork)
Spinach & FetaSpinach, tangy fetaA slightly grown-up twist

How Much You Get, and What It Costs

A single order comes cut into 8 pieces, which works as a shared appetizer for two to four people or a generous snack for one hungry person who isn't sharing (no judgment). On price, here's the good news: Stuffed Cheesy Bread frequently qualifies for the $6.99 Each and Mix & Match deals, which is comfortably the cheapest way to add it to an order. Tacking it onto a pizza through a deal is one of those little moves that makes the whole meal feel bigger without the total jumping much. Peek at the current deals before you order.

Nutrition and Allergens

Each piece runs roughly 140 to 180 calories depending on the variety, so it's a treat rather than a health food — but you knew that. It contains wheat and milk, and the bacon-jalapeño version adds pork. Good to know on the dips, too: the marinara is vegetarian-friendly, while ranch and garlic dips contain milk and egg. If you're sharing across a few people, one order stretches further than you'd expect, which helps on both calories and cost.

What to Pair It With

Stuffed Cheesy Bread is the classic wingman to a good pizza. It's the natural companion to a Pepperoni or the loaded ExtravaganZZa. For a full family spread, add a 2-liter of Coke and run the whole order through Mix & Match so the side basically pays for itself in savings. It also gives the non-pizza eater at the table something to reach for, which every family knows is worth its weight in gold.

The Bottom Line

Stuffed Cheesy Bread is proof that the best part of a Domino's order isn't always the pizza. Gooey, shareable, and cheap when you grab it inside a deal — it's an easy yes on almost any order. Prices here are examples, so let the official Domino's app confirm the real number at checkout. This is an independent, unofficial guide, but the recommendation is heartfelt: get the cheesy bread.

title: Domino's Boneless Chicken
description: Lightly breaded, oven-baked all-white-meat boneless chicken, served plain or tossed in a signature sauce.
fullContent:
The Most Versatile Thing on the Menu

Here's a little secret: Boneless Chicken might be the most flexible order at Domino's. It's lightly breaded, oven-baked, all-white-meat chicken that you can grab plain with a dip or tossed in a sauce. Want an appetizer? Done. A lighter main instead of pizza? Also done. A protein boost alongside a pie through a deal? That too. Not many items pull triple duty like this, and that's exactly why it's a smart thing to keep in your back pocket.

And to clear up a common mix-up — yes, boneless chicken is genuinely boneless. It's white-meat chicken with no bones, which makes it completely different from Domino's bone-in wings. No gnawing, no mess, just easy pieces you can dunk and go.

Pick Your Sauce

This is where boneless chicken gets fun, because the sauce completely changes the personality of the order.

SauceThe Vibe
Plain (with a dip)Simple, kid-friendly, you control the flavor
Hot BuffaloClassic tangy heat
Sweet BBQSweet, smoky, crowd-pleasing
Garlic ParmesanSavory and rich
Mango HabaneroSweet up front, spicy on the finish

My move for a mixed group? Order it plain and let everyone dip it their own way. For myself, it's Sweet BBQ every time, no debate.

Portions and Smart Pricing

Domino's serves Boneless Chicken in an 8-piece order and larger shareable counts. An 8-piece works nicely as a solo meal or a side for two. Here's the value angle that makes it a favorite of mine: it's one of the best Mix & Match and $6.99 Each picks going, because it rounds out a pizza order with real protein for a low add-on cost. When a pizza alone won't quite satisfy the table, a deal-priced order of boneless chicken fixes it cheaply. Check the current deals and stay in Rewards while you're at it.

Nutrition and Allergens

Plain Boneless Chicken runs roughly 60 to 70 calories per piece before any sauce, which makes it one of the lighter ways to add protein to a Domino's order — order it plain and it's genuinely reasonable. The sauces add calories and sodium, and the Sweet BBQ and Mango Habanero are the sugariest of the bunch, so keep that in mind if you're watching intake. On allergens, it contains wheat, milk, soy and egg from the breading, so it isn't gluten-free despite being 'just chicken.'

What to Pair It With

Boneless chicken slots into almost any order. Pair it with a Pepperoni Pizza and a drink for the classic combo, or use it as the protein in a lighter meal alongside a thin-crust veggie pizza. Add Stuffed Cheesy Bread and you've built a proper shareable spread. For the full lineup of chicken and everything else, the menu and prices page has it all.

The Bottom Line

Boneless Chicken is the quiet workhorse of the Domino's menu — flexible, deal-friendly, and lighter than most sides when you keep it plain. It's the easiest way to turn 'just a pizza' into a real meal without spending much. As always, prices are examples, so let the official Domino's app confirm the real total. This is an independent, unofficial guide, here to help you order well.

title: Domino's Drinks Menu & Prices
description: Coca-Cola fountain products in 20 oz bottles and 2-liter bottles to round out any Domino's order.
fullContent:
Don't Overthink the Drinks (But Do Read This)

The drinks are the easiest part of any Domino's order, but there's one small decision that quietly saves you money, and most people get it wrong. Domino's stocks a lineup of Coca-Cola beverages in two formats: individual 20 oz bottles and shareable 2-liter bottles. That's the whole choice, really. But because drinks are franchise-priced and vary more than almost anything else on the menu, picking the right size is where you either save a couple of bucks or hand them over for no reason.

What's on Offer

The core lineup covers the classics, though exact availability comes down to what your local store keeps in stock.

Drink20 oz Calories (approx.)Best For
Coca-Cola~240The timeless pizza pairing
Diet Coke~0Classic taste, no sugar
Coke Zero Sugar~0Closest to regular, sugar-free
Sprite~240Crisp and citrusy
Fanta Orange~240Sweet, fun, kid-approved
Barq's Root Beer~250Something a little different

The One Rule: Get the 2-Liter

Here's the whole money tip in one line. If you're ordering for two or more people, the 2-liter bottle is almost always cheaper per ounce than buying individual 20 oz bottles, and it's not even close. Six people, six bottles? That adds up fast and creates a pile of plastic. One 2-liter covers the same crowd for less and takes up one spot in the bag. It's the single easiest saving on the drinks menu, and sometimes drinks even qualify as an item in the Mix & Match deal, so check the current offers before you add one.

The 20 oz bottles have their place, of course — grab one when it's just you and you want your own cold drink without half a liter left over. Right size, right situation.

Watching the Sugar

Let's be real about it: a 20 oz regular Coca-Cola packs roughly 240 calories, which is a fair chunk to drink without noticing. If you're keeping an eye on sugar, Diet Coke and Coke Zero Sugar are effectively calorie-free, and Coke Zero in particular gets you close to the real thing. Sprite and Fanta land in the same ballpark as regular Coke on calories, so they're a treat rather than a freebie. No lectures here — just know what you're pouring so you can choose on purpose.

What to Pair It With

Honestly, any of these works with any pizza — that's the beauty of it. But the timeless move is a Coke next to a Pepperoni Pizza and some Stuffed Cheesy Bread. For a family order, a 2-liter is the glue that ties the whole meal together for cheap. There's more on building a complete family spread in the family picks guide, and the full lineup lives on the menu and prices page.

The Bottom Line

Drinks are simple: pick your flavor, and get the 2-liter if you're feeding more than one person. That's the whole strategy. Prices vary by store more than most items, so these are examples only — let the official Domino's app confirm the real total at checkout. This is an independent, unofficial guide, and on drinks, the advice is short and sweet: go big on the bottle, save on the total.

title: Domino's Chicken Alfredo Pasta
description: Penne baked with grilled chicken breast in a creamy Alfredo sauce, served in a dish or inside a hollowed-out bread bowl.
fullContent:
What It Is

Chicken Alfredo is Domino's most popular pasta and the one most people default to. It is penne tossed with grilled chicken breast in a creamy Alfredo sauce, then baked in the same conveyor oven as the pizzas rather than boiled and plated. That oven finish is what gives the top a slightly browned, bubbling edge that you don't get from pasta reheated in a pan.

Dish or Bread Bowl?

This is the only real decision, and it matters more than the pasta choice itself.

Served InExample PriceCalories
Dish~$7.99~620
Bread bowl~$8.99~980

The bread bowl is a round loaf hollowed out and baked with the pasta inside, so the bowl itself is edible. It adds roughly a dollar and around 360 calories — you are effectively ordering a large bread roll alongside your meal. It is genuinely fun once, and if you are properly hungry it turns a modest portion into a heavy one. But if pasta felt like the sensible choice next to pizza, the bread bowl quietly cancels that out.

How It Tastes

Rich, mild and heavily cheese-forward. The Alfredo is a thick cream sauce rather than a thin one, so it clings to the penne and the chicken instead of pooling at the bottom. There is no chilli heat at all, which makes it the safe pick for children or anyone who finds the marinara-based options too sharp.

The chicken is grilled breast meat, diced rather than shredded. It is the lean part of an otherwise rich dish, and it is the reason this reads as a meal rather than a side.

Who It Suits

  • Someone who doesn't want pizza but is ordering with a group that does
  • Lunch — the dish version travels well and needs no sharing
  • Children — mild, familiar, no heat
  • Not anyone watching calories closely — even the dish is around 620, and the bread bowl clears 950

Ordering Notes

A few things worth knowing before you tap order:

  • It is Mix & Match eligible at most stores. Ordering it inside a deal alongside a pizza is normally cheaper than adding it at menu price — see our Mix & Match explainer.
  • You can build your own instead. If you want the Alfredo base with different additions, the build-your-own penne lets you pick the sauce and up to three toppings.
  • It contains dairy throughout. The Alfredo sauce is cream-based, so there is no dairy-free version of this dish — see our vegetarian and vegan guide for what works instead.
  • Reheats poorly in a microwave. Cream sauces split. An oven at low heat holds it together far better.

How It Compares

Against the other pastas: Chicken Carbonara is richer and heavier, Italian Sausage Marinara is the tomato-based alternative, and Pasta Primavera is the lightest and the only vegetarian one. Full prices and calories for all of them are in our sides menu guide.

Prices on this page are examples for guidance. Domino's stores set their own prices, so the checkout screen is the only figure that counts.

title: Domino's Italian Sausage Marinara Pasta
description: Penne baked with Italian sausage in a hearty marinara sauce, available in a dish or a bread bowl.
fullContent:
What It Is

This is the tomato-based option in Domino's pasta lineup: penne baked with crumbled Italian sausage in a hearty marinara, finished with cheese. It sits opposite Chicken Alfredo on the menu — where Alfredo is cream and mild, this is tomato and seasoned.

Prices and Calories

Served InExample PriceCalories
Dish~$7.99~580
Bread bowl~$8.99~940

Notice that the dish is around 40 calories lighter than the Alfredo — that is the tomato sauce doing its job. It is not a big gap, but if you are choosing between the two on those grounds, marinara is the lighter one.

How It Tastes

Italian sausage is the whole point here. It is crumbled rather than sliced, so it distributes through the pasta instead of sitting in lumps, and it carries fennel and black pepper. That gives the dish a savoury, slightly herby edge that the marinara alone wouldn't have.

People often ask whether it is spicy. It isn't, in the chilli sense — the heat is seasoning, not burn. If you want actual heat you'd need to build your own and add jalapeños.

Who It Suits

  • Anyone who finds cream sauces heavy — this is the alternative
  • People who want the pasta to taste of something beyond cheese
  • A group order where someone has already claimed the Alfredo
  • Not vegetarians — the sausage is central, and there is no meat-free version of this recipe

Ordering Notes

  • Skip the bread bowl if calories matter. It adds roughly 360, taking a mid-weight dish to almost a thousand.
  • Mix & Match eligible at most stores, which is nearly always cheaper than ordering it standalone next to a full-price pizza.
  • Reheats better than Alfredo. Tomato sauces survive a microwave; cream sauces split. If leftovers are likely, this is the more forgiving choice.
  • Build-your-own alternative: choose Robust Inspired Tomato Sauce and add your own toppings if you want the marinara base without sausage.

How It Compares

Marinara versus Alfredo is the real question, and it comes down to whether you want cream or tomato. Chicken Carbonara is the richest of the four at around 660 in a dish, and Pasta Primavera is the lightest at roughly 490 and the only vegetarian one. Our sides menu guide has all four side by side, and the calories guide puts them in context against the pizzas.

title: Domino's Pasta Primavera
description: The vegetarian pasta — penne baked with vegetables in a creamy sauce, and the lightest of Domino's four pasta dishes.
fullContent:
What It Is

Pasta Primavera is the vegetarian entry in Domino's pasta range: penne baked with vegetables in a creamy sauce. It is also, by a clear margin, the lightest of the four pastas — roughly 490 calories in a dish against 620 for Chicken Alfredo and about 660 for Chicken Carbonara.

Prices and Calories

Served InExample PriceCalories
Dish~$7.99~490
Bread bowl~$8.99~850

Worth pausing on those two rows. The bread bowl adds about 360 calories — nearly as much again as the pasta itself. If you chose Primavera because it was the light option, the dish is the version that keeps that promise.

How It Tastes

Vegetable-forward but still creamy — this is not a tomato pasta. The vegetables soften in the oven rather than staying crunchy, and the sauce binds everything together. It is milder than the sausage marinara and lighter than the Alfredo, which puts it in a genuinely useful middle position rather than making it a compromise.

Vegetarian, Not Vegan

This matters and it gets confused often. Pasta Primavera contains no meat, so it works for vegetarians. It is not vegan — the sauce and cheese are dairy-based, and Domino's prepares everything in a shared kitchen with shared surfaces and utensils.

If you are vegan, the workable route is a build-your-own penne with Robust Inspired Tomato Sauce, vegetable toppings and no cheese. Our vegetarian and vegan guide walks through that in full, including which crusts and sauces qualify.

Who It Suits

  • The one vegetarian in a group ordering pizza — this is a proper meal, not an afterthought
  • Anyone counting calories who still wants something hot and filling
  • Lunch, where a full pizza is too much
  • Not anyone avoiding dairy — the sauce rules it out

Ordering Notes

  • Order the dish, not the bowl, if the calorie count is why you picked it
  • Mix & Match eligible at most stores — cheaper inside a deal than beside one
  • Pair it with a garden salad rather than a bread side if you want to keep the meal light
  • Check the vegetable mix at your store, since recipes vary slightly by market

title: Domino's Philly Cheese Steak Sandwich
description: Oven-baked sandwich with steak, onions, green peppers, mushrooms and a provolone and American cheese blend on artisan bread.
fullContent:
The Most Overlooked Thing on the Menu

Domino's sandwiches get almost no attention, and that is a shame, because they are the reason Domino's works as a lunch stop rather than only a dinner one. They are baked on artisan bread in the same conveyor oven as the pizzas, which is why they arrive properly hot instead of sitting under a lamp.

The Philly Cheese Steak is the flagship. It is sliced steak with onions, green peppers and mushrooms under a blend of provolone and American cheese.

Price and Portion

ItemExample PriceCalories
Philly Cheese Steak Sandwich~$7.99~700–900
Small pizza, for comparison~$8.99~1,200

That comparison is the useful one. For one person eating alone, a sandwich is often the smarter buy than a small pizza — similar money, no leftovers going stale in a box, and it survives the trip better.

On the calorie figure: 700 to 900 is an honest range rather than a precise number. Sandwich nutrition varies more between recipes than pizza does, so if it matters, read the live figure in the app.

How It Tastes

Savoury and cheese-heavy, with no tomato sauce anywhere. The two cheeses do different jobs — provolone for stretch and American for the melt — and the vegetables soften in the oven rather than staying crisp. The steak is sliced thin, so it reads as part of the filling rather than as a separate piece of meat.

If you like the Philly Cheese Steak pizza, this is the same flavour profile in a more portable format. If you have never tried either, this is the least pizza-like thing Domino's makes, and that is exactly its appeal on a day when you don't want pizza.

Who It Suits

  • Solo lunch — the single best use case, no sharing and no leftovers
  • Someone in the group who doesn't want pizza
  • Carryout orders, where it arrives at its best
  • Not vegetarians — the Mediterranean Veggie is the meat-free sandwich

Ordering Notes

  • Sandwiches are usually Mix & Match eligible. Adding one inside a deal costs less than adding it at menu price — see our Mix & Match explainer.
  • Eat it hot. The melted cheese is the whole structure of the thing; cold it becomes solid.
  • Add a dipping cup if you like — marinara is the light one at around 45 calories against 100 to 170 for the creamy dips.
  • Check the current deals before paying, since sandwich pricing moves with promotions. Our coupons page tracks what is running.

Prices here are examples. Domino's stores are individually franchised and set their own prices — always verify at checkout. The rest of the non-pizza menu is covered in our sides menu guide.

title: Domino's Chicken Bacon Ranch Sandwich
description: Oven-baked sandwich with grilled chicken, smoked bacon, creamy ranch and provolone on artisan bread.
fullContent:
What It Is

Grilled chicken breast, smoked bacon, creamy ranch and provolone, baked on artisan bread. It is the richest of Domino's sandwiches and the closest thing on the menu to straightforward comfort food.

Price and Calories

ItemExample PriceCalories
Chicken Bacon Ranch Sandwich~$7.99~700–900

As with all the sandwiches, treat that calorie band as approximate. It is a real range rather than a precise count, and the app will give you the exact figure for your store's recipe.

How It Tastes

Ranch is the dominant note, and whether that appeals to you decides the whole sandwich. It is creamy, tangy and mild — there is no heat in it at all. The bacon supplies smoke and salt, the chicken keeps it from being purely rich, and the provolone melts into the sauce rather than sitting on top of it.

If you have had the Cali Chicken Bacon Ranch pizza, this is the same idea in sandwich form. Both are built on ranch instead of tomato sauce, which is the single most surprising thing on Domino's menu for anyone who has only ordered red-sauce pizzas.

Who It Suits

  • Anyone who likes ranch — this is the most ranch-forward item Domino's makes
  • Solo lunch or a late-night order
  • Children — mild, no heat, familiar flavours
  • Not anyone avoiding dairy or egg — the ranch rules out both
  • Not the choice if you want heat; look at the habanero or buffalo options where your store carries them

Ordering Notes

  • Order it hot and eat it hot. Ranch and melted provolone are excellent warm and unpleasant cold.
  • Mix & Match eligible at most stores — building it into a larger order is cheaper than adding it at the end.
  • Skip the extra ranch cup. The sandwich already carries the sauce, and a dipping cup adds roughly 170 calories on top.
  • Allergen check: ranch typically contains egg as well as dairy. Domino's publishes an allergen guide, and that is the source worth reading rather than any third-party page.

How It Compares

Against the Philly Cheese Steak, this is the creamier and less savoury of the two — Philly is steak and vegetables, this is chicken and sauce. The Mediterranean Veggie is the vegetarian alternative. All the sandwich prices sit in the same $6.99 to $8.99 band, so the choice is about flavour rather than value.

title: Domino's Mediterranean Veggie Sandwich
description: The vegetarian sandwich — spinach, feta, banana peppers, onions and tomatoes baked on artisan bread.
fullContent:
The Vegetarian Sandwich

This is the only meat-free sandwich Domino's makes: baby spinach, feta, banana peppers, onions and tomatoes with provolone, baked on artisan bread. If you are vegetarian and someone else has ordered pizza, this is your hot alternative to picking at a side.

Price and Calories

ItemExample PriceCalories
Mediterranean Veggie Sandwich~$8.99~700–900
Other sandwiches~$6.99–$7.99~700–900

It commonly lists a little higher than the meat sandwiches, which surprises people. Feta and the vegetable mix are the usual reason. Whether that is worth a dollar is your call, but it is the only option in this category if you don't eat meat.

How It Tastes

Brighter and sharper than the other two sandwiches. Feta is doing most of the work — it is salty and tangy in a way mozzarella isn't, and it stops a vegetable sandwich from tasting flat. The banana peppers add acidity rather than heat; they are tangy, not hot, which people frequently expect wrongly.

The spinach wilts down in the oven, so do not expect a fresh salad texture. This is a baked, soft, savoury sandwich, and it is better for it.

Vegetarian, Not Vegan

Worth being precise about. It contains no meat, so it works for vegetarians. It is not vegan — both the feta and the provolone are dairy, and Domino's prepares everything in a shared kitchen on shared surfaces.

There is currently no vegan sandwich on the US menu. If you are vegan, the practical options are a cheeseless build-your-own pizza or a build-your-own pasta with tomato sauce. Our vegetarian and vegan guide covers exactly what qualifies and what doesn't.

Who It Suits

  • The vegetarian in a mixed group order — its main reason to exist
  • Anyone who finds the ranch and cheese sandwiches too heavy
  • People who like feta and briny flavours
  • Not vegans, and not anyone expecting the banana peppers to be spicy

Ordering Notes

  • Usually Mix & Match eligible, which offsets the slightly higher menu price
  • Eat it hot — the feta and provolone set as it cools
  • Pair it with a garden salad rather than a bread side to keep the meal from being carbohydrate on carbohydrate
  • Check availability — the sandwich lineup varies more by market than the pizza menu does

title: Domino's Chocolate Lava Crunch Cakes
description: Two warm chocolate cakes with a molten chocolate centre — Domino's best-known dessert.
fullContent:
The Dessert People Actually Order

Domino's dessert menu is short, and the Chocolate Lava Crunch Cakes are the reason most people look at it. Two warm chocolate cakes with a molten chocolate centre, baked so the middle stays liquid.

Price and Calories

ItemPortionExample PriceCalories
Chocolate Lava Crunch Cakes2 cakes~$4.99~350 each
Cinnamon Bread Twists8 pieces~$5.99~250 / 2 pc
Marbled Cookie Brownie9 pieces~$6.99~200 / piece

They are the cheapest dessert on the menu and the one that splits most cleanly — two cakes, two people, no negotiation. Eating both yourself is roughly 700 calories, which is worth knowing before you decide.

Getting Them at Their Best

This is the one dessert on the menu where timing genuinely matters. The molten centre firms up as the cake cools, so a lava cake eaten twenty minutes after delivery is a decent chocolate cake, while one eaten immediately is the thing you actually ordered.

Two practical consequences:

  • Carryout beats a long delivery for these specifically
  • Eat them before the pizza cools if delivery took a while — counterintuitive, but the cakes are more time-sensitive than the pizza is

If they have gone cold, a short warm-up in an oven restores the centre far better than a microwave, which tends to make the cake rubbery.

Who It Suits

  • Two people — the portion is designed for exactly this
  • Anyone wanting dessert without ordering a whole tray of something
  • Carryout orders, where they arrive properly warm
  • Not a group of four or more — order the Cinnamon Bread Twists or the Cookie Brownie instead, which divide properly
  • Not vegans — they contain dairy and egg, and there is no vegan dessert on the US menu

Ordering Notes

  • Usually Mix & Match eligible, so adding them inside a deal costs less than tacking them on at menu price
  • They contain wheat, dairy and egg — check Domino's allergen guide if that matters to you
  • Don't over-order. One pair between two is plenty; two pairs between two is a lot of chocolate

Prices are examples for guidance only — Domino's stores price independently, so verify at checkout. The full dessert and sides lineup is in our sides menu guide, and calorie context across the whole menu is in the nutrition guide.

title: Domino's Cinnamon Bread Twists
description: Eight freshly baked bread twists dusted with cinnamon and sugar, served with sweet icing.
fullContent:
The Dessert for a Group

Cinnamon Bread Twists are the same twisted bread as Domino's savoury sides, baked golden and then dusted with cinnamon and sugar, with a cup of sweet icing for dipping. Eight pieces to an order, which is what makes them the sharing option.

Price and Portion

DessertPiecesExample PriceFeeds
Cinnamon Bread Twists8~$5.993–4 people
Lava Crunch Cakes2~$4.992 people
Marbled Cookie Brownie9~$6.994–5 people

That is the honest way to choose between the three: pick by how many people you are feeding, not by flavour. Two lava cakes between four means somebody misses out; eight twists divides cleanly.

Calories — Read This Bit

Roughly 250 calories per two pieces, which sounds modest until you do the arithmetic. A full eight-piece order is around 1,000 calories, and that is before the icing cup.

They are easy to eat without noticing, in the way a shared plate of bread always is. Shared between three or four people it is a reasonable dessert; eaten solo it is a second meal. Our calories guide puts that in context against the rest of the menu.

How They Taste

Soft rather than crisp, with cinnamon sugar on the outside and a plain bread interior. They are sweeter through the coating than the dough — the twist itself is fairly neutral, which is why the icing cup matters. Dipped, they are properly sweet; undipped, they are closer to a cinnamon roll without the glaze.

They hold up better than the lava cakes on a long delivery, since there is no molten centre to set. That makes them the safer dessert if your store is far away.

Who It Suits

  • Groups of three or four — the portion divides properly
  • Long deliveries, where lava cakes would arrive cold
  • Anyone who prefers bread-based desserts to cake
  • Not vegans — they contain milk, like all of Domino's bread sides
  • Not the best solo order; the portion is too big for one

Ordering Notes

  • Mix & Match eligible at most stores — cheaper inside a deal than added at the end
  • Ask for the icing on the side if you'd rather control the sweetness; it usually comes that way
  • They reheat reasonably — a few minutes in an oven brings them back, unlike cream-based items
  • Treat them as replacing a side, not adding to one, if you have already ordered bread with the meal

Prices shown are examples. Domino's stores are individually franchised — confirm at official checkout.

title: Domino's Marbled Cookie Brownie
description: A baked tray of marbled cookie and brownie, cut into nine pieces — the dessert that feeds a group.
fullContent:
The Group Dessert

The Marbled Cookie Brownie is exactly what the name says: cookie dough and brownie batter swirled together, baked as a tray and cut into nine pieces. It is the largest dessert portion on the menu and the only one that comfortably feeds four or five people.

Price and Portion

DessertPiecesExample PriceCal / Piece
Marbled Cookie Brownie9~$6.99~200
Cinnamon Bread Twists8~$5.99~125
Lava Crunch Cakes2~$4.99~350

Per piece it is the middle option on calories and the most expensive per order — but per person it is the cheapest way to give five people dessert. One tray covers a table that two lava cakes would not.

The whole tray is roughly 1,800 calories, which is the number worth knowing if it ends up sitting on the coffee table during a film.

How It Tastes

Because the batter is marbled rather than layered, each piece carries both textures — the chew of a cookie and the denser, fudgier brownie running through it. The result is sweeter and denser than the bread twists and less dramatic than a lava cake, with no molten centre to lose.

That last point is a practical advantage. It survives delivery better than anything else on the dessert menu. There is nothing time-sensitive about it, so a long delivery does not spoil it the way it spoils lava cakes.

Who It Suits

  • Four or five people — the only Domino's dessert that stretches that far
  • Long deliveries, since nothing about it depends on arriving hot
  • Parties and film nights, where a tray beats individual portions
  • Not one or two people — you will be eating brownie for two days
  • Not vegans; it contains dairy and egg

Ordering Notes

  • Mix & Match eligible at most stores, which is where the value is — added at menu price next to a full-price pizza, it is the most expensive dessert
  • Keeps well. Unlike the rest of the menu, leftovers are genuinely fine the next day
  • Contains wheat, dairy and egg — check the official allergen guide if that matters
  • Order it instead of, not alongside, a bread side unless you are feeding a real crowd

Choosing Between the Three

Simple rule: two people order lava cakes, three or four order cinnamon twists, five or more order the brownie. Flavour preference matters less than portion here, because all three are sweet, shareable and priced within two dollars of each other.

title: Domino's Parmesan Bread Bites
description: Sixteen small baked bread bites brushed with garlic and Parmesan — the best value side on the menu.
fullContent:
The Best Value Side on the Menu

Sixteen small baked bread bites, brushed with garlic seasoning and Parmesan, for around $4.99. Per piece, nothing else on the Domino's menu comes close on value, and the portion is the easiest to pass around a table without anyone measuring their share.

Price Against the Other Bread Sides

SidePiecesExample PriceCalories
Parmesan Bread Bites16~$4.99~220 / 4 pc
Garlic Bread Twists8~$5.99~220 / 2 pc
Stuffed Cheesy Bread8~$7.99~260 / 2 pc

Two things stand out. The bites are the cheapest order and the largest piece count. And per calorie they are the lightest way into the bread category — 220 for four small bites against 260 for two pieces of Stuffed Cheesy Bread.

That said, a full sixteen-piece order is roughly 880 calories, so "lightest" is relative. They are easy to eat absent-mindedly.

How They Taste

Small, soft and garlicky, with Parmesan on the outside rather than inside. They are closer to seasoned dinner rolls than to breadsticks — there is no crisp shell, and no cheese pull, because there is no cheese filling.

Because each piece is small, they work far better for sharing than the twists do. Sixteen pieces around four people is four each; eight twists around four people is two each and immediately awkward.

Dipping Sauce Matters Here

The bites are fairly plain on their own, so the dip does real work. Worth knowing what each one costs you:

  • Marinara — around 45 calories a cup, the light choice
  • Ranch or blue cheese — roughly 100 to 170 a cup
  • Garlic and butter style dips — the heaviest of the lot

If you are having two or three cups with a shared bread side, that is a meaningful number sitting quietly next to your pizza. Marinara is the freebie in calorie terms.

Who It Suits

  • Sharing around a table of three or four — the portion divides best of any side
  • Ordering on a budget — the cheapest way to add something to a pizza order
  • Children, since the pieces are small and mild
  • Not anyone wanting the cheese-pull experience — that is Stuffed Cheesy Bread
  • Not vegans; all Domino's bread sides contain milk

Ordering Notes

  • Mix & Match eligible at most stores, which makes an already cheap side cheaper
  • One shared side per three or four people is the rule that stops food going home in a box
  • They cool quickly because the pieces are small — worth eating early in the meal

title: Domino's Garlic Bread Twists
description: Eight freshly baked bread twists brushed with garlic and butter-flavoured seasoning, served with marinara.
fullContent:
What It Is

Eight lengths of bread dough, twisted, baked, and brushed with garlic and a butter-flavoured seasoning, served with a marinara cup. This is the plainest, most familiar side Domino's makes — no filling, no cheese layer, just garlic bread in a twisted shape.

Price and Calories

SidePiecesExample PriceCal / 2 pc
Garlic Bread Twists8~$5.99~220
Parmesan Bread Twists8~$5.99~230
Parmesan Bread Bites16~$4.99~110

The comparison worth making is with the bites. The bites are cheaper, and there are twice as many pieces — so if you are feeding a group, they are the better buy. The twists win on format: they are substantial enough to eat as a proper side rather than a nibble, and they dip better.

Garlic or Parmesan?

The two twist varieties are the same bread with a different finish. Garlic is brushed with seasoning and butter flavour. Parmesan adds cheese on top and comes out roughly ten calories heavier per two pieces.

In practice: garlic is the better partner for a pizza that already has a lot going on, and Parmesan is better if the bread is doing more of the work in the meal. The price is normally identical, so this is purely taste.

Calories in Context

Around 220 per two pieces means a full order is roughly 880 calories — close to half a large cheese pizza. That is the thing people underestimate about bread sides. They read as "a side" and they eat like a course.

The practical fix is not to skip them but to let them replace pizza rather than accompany it. One bread side plus two fewer slices lands in the same place as three slices, and the table enjoys it more. Our calories guide has the full comparison.

Who It Suits

  • Two or three people sharing alongside a pizza
  • Anyone who wants plain garlic bread rather than a cheese-filled side
  • Dipping — the twist shape holds sauce better than bites do
  • Not a big group; sixteen bites divide better than eight twists
  • Not vegans — they contain milk

Ordering Notes

  • Mix & Match eligible at most stores — always cheaper inside a deal than beside one
  • Marinara is the light dip at around 45 calories against 100 to 170 for the creamy ones
  • Eat them hot. Bread sides firm up noticeably as they cool
  • Check what your pizza already has. If you have ordered Parmesan Stuffed Crust, another garlic bread side is a lot of the same flavour

title: Domino's Loaded Tots
description: Crispy potato tots baked with cheese and toppings, in three versions — Cheddar Bacon, Melty 3-Cheese and Philly Cheese Steak.
fullContent:
The Newest Side

Loaded Tots are the most recent addition to this part of Domino's menu: crispy potato tots baked with sauce and cheese on top, in three versions. They are the only non-bread, non-chicken hot side on the menu, which is the main reason to order them.

The Three Versions

VersionWhat's On ThemCal / Quarter
Cheddar BaconBacon, mozzarella, cheddar, garlic Parmesan sauce~240
Melty 3-CheeseMozzarella, cheddar, provolone, Alfredo~210
Philly Cheese SteakSteak, onions, green peppers, Alfredo, cheese blend~200

All three are normally the same price — commonly around $6.99 as part of a Mix & Match order. Philly Cheese Steak is both the lightest and the most substantial in terms of actual filling, which makes it the pick if you are choosing on merit rather than on cheese volume.

The Honest Verdict on Delivery

This needs saying plainly, because it decides whether you enjoy them. Tots travel worse than bread does. Crispiness is the entire appeal, and twenty minutes in a sealed container with hot cheese on top steams it away.

  • On carryout: genuinely good — crisp outside, molten on top
  • On a short delivery: fine
  • On a long delivery: soft, and you will wonder what the fuss was about

If your store is far away, order bread instead and save the tots for a pickup run. Our carryout deals guide covers where pickup wins on price too, which makes this an easy trade.

How They Taste

Familiar, in a good way — these are recognisably potato tots, not a reinvention. The sauces are the differentiator: garlic Parmesan on the Cheddar Bacon gives it a savoury, garlicky edge, while the Alfredo versions are creamier and milder. None of the three is spicy.

Who It Suits

  • Carryout orders — the format they are built for
  • Anyone bored of bread sides, which until recently was the only real option
  • Sharing between two; a portion divides into about four servings
  • Not long-delivery orders
  • Not vegans — all three versions carry dairy

Ordering Notes

  • Usually Mix & Match eligible, which is where the $6.99 price comes from — standalone they cost more
  • Availability varies. As a newer item, not every store carries all three versions
  • Don't stack them with a bread side. Both are heavy starch; pick one
  • Eat them first if they arrive with a pizza — they are the most time-sensitive thing in the bag

Prices shown are examples for guidance. Domino's stores are individually franchised and price independently — always confirm at official checkout.

faqs.question: What flavours do Domino's Loaded Tots come in?
faqs.answer: Three — Cheddar Bacon, Melty 3-Cheese and Philly Cheese Steak. All are usually priced the same, commonly around $6.99 in a Mix & Match order.

faqs.question: How many calories are in Loaded Tots?
faqs.answer: Roughly 200 to 240 per quarter portion depending on the version, with Cheddar Bacon the heaviest and Philly Cheese Steak the lightest.

faqs.question: Do Loaded Tots travel well?
faqs.answer: Not especially. Tots are at their best straight from the oven, and a long delivery softens them. They are a much better carryout order.
